questions_frozen.question: Does Albertsons hold its FY26 adjusted EPS guide of $1.75-1.85 (and adjusted EBITDA $3.550-3.625B) at the Q2 print, rather than cutting it a second time?
questions_frozen.why_it_decides: The stock trades on the guide: on 2026-07-23 it fell 21.6% when the FY26 EPS guide was cut from $2.22-2.32 to $1.75-1.85 and IDs from 0/+1% to -1.5/-0.5%, a larger move than the quarter miss alone ($0.42 vs $0.54) warranted. A second cut inside one quarter of a reset would break the 'kitchen-sink' narrative; a hold removes the tail the skew is paying for.
questions_frozen.priced_answer: Mixed. Yahoo consensus FY (Feb-27) EPS $1.792 (n=19, range $1.65-1.912), flat for 60 days, sits on the guide midpoint ($1.80) - the bulk of the street holds 'guide maintained'. Zacks/Nasdaq (n=6) carries $1.65, below the low end. Options: event implied 6.22% with 25d skew +4.7 (downside paid); short interest 59.5M = 18.15% of float, up 9% m/m into the print (Yahoo, settlement 2026-09-30). So the consensus number says hold, the positioning says a cut is feared.
questions_frozen.resolved_by: The fiscal 2026 outlook table in the Q2 release (adj EPS, adj EBITDA, IDs) and CFO commentary on the call.

questions_frozen.question: Do Q2 identical sales (12 weeks to ~2026-09-12) come in at -1.0% or better including the ~150bp IRA pharmacy headwind, i.e. is the ex-IRA grocery trend steady or better than Q1's ~+0.7%?
questions_frozen.why_it_decides: Q1's -0.8% ID (ex-IRA/deflation ~+0.7%) and the unit-softness commentary drove the July cut; management promised 'very modest improvement each quarter' in grocery while pharmacy laps tougher compares from Q2. The ID line is the first read on whether the reset was enough.
questions_frozen.priced_answer: No sourced ID consensus found at freeze. Revenue consensus $18.86B (n=15, $18.68-19.10B) vs $18.92B a year ago (-0.3%), with fuel prices ~+27% y/y lifting the top line, implies the street models IDs around -1% or a bit worse. Guide range for FY is -1.5% to -0.5%.
questions_frozen.resolved_by: Identical sales line and the pharmacy/IRA bridge in the release; quarter-to-date (Q3) ID commentary on the call.
